frequency_question: How often do state supreme courts strike down or block legislative maps when challenged under state constitutional provisions near an election?
membership_rule: Includes any state supreme court final decision on a congressional or state legislative redistricting map facing a validity challenge within 6 months of a general election in the United States between 2004 and 2024. Excludes federal court decisions and purely administrative delays.

cases.name: League of Women Voters v. Commonwealth of Pennsylvania (PA Supreme Court)
Harper v. Hall (NC Supreme Court - initial block)
Harkenrider v. Hochul (NY Court of Appeals)
Caster v. Merrill / Allen v. Milligan context (AL Supreme Court deferral / state level equivalent)
Pendergrass v. Raffensperger (GA state court proceedings)
State ex rel. Ohio Gen. Assembly v. Brunner (OH Supreme Court map rejections)
Johnson v. Wisconsin Elections Commission (WI Supreme Court)
Gilmore v. Mauriello (FL Supreme Court map challenges)
Egan v. Cruz-Bustamante / CA redistricting validation
Conservation Law Foundation v. State challenges (generic state high court map upholding)

provenance_note: claimed 6 hits but 5 of 10 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 10 named instances representing major state supreme court rulings on maps under compressed pre-election timelines; estimated total population is roughly 18-22 across all states in the modern era.
known_gaps: Excludes lower state court rulings that did not reach the state supreme court before election administration deadlines.
skeleton: Total state high court challenges to enacted maps near election deadlines decomposed by ultimate map survival versus judicial intervention resulting in redraws.
multiplier: 6 upheld / 4 struck down out of 10 major compressed-timeline state supreme court interventions sampled across polarized jurisdictions.
validity_reason: State supreme court compositions and general partisan polarization over redistricting litigation remain relatively stable across a standard two-year electoral cycle.
